This petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. is filed by the petitioners - accused Nos.1 to 3 challenging the proceedings in C.C.No.2093/2020, on the file of the I Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, at Kalaburagi, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504 and 506 read with 34 of IPC.
02.
The case of the prosecution is that, the accused No.1 is the husband of the de-facto complainant,
accused
Nos.2 and 3 are the parents in law.
They had subjected the de-facto - complainant to cruelty both mentally and physically.
The learned Magistrate after accepting the charge- sheet, took the cognizance of the aforesaid offences and issued summons.
Taking exception of the same, this petition is filed.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the petitioners - accused Nos.1 to 3 submits that, except omnibus and general allegations, there is no specific allegation as against each of the petitioners - accused Nos.1 to 3.
As such, the cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate only on the basis of omnibus and general allegations, is impermissible.
05. The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 - de- facto complainant submits that, the charge-sheet material discloses the commission of the offences by the petitioners - accused Nos.1 to 3.
The veracity of the allegations alleged against the petitioners - accused Nos.1 to 3, can be considered at the time of trial.
Hence, the present petition is not maintainable.
06. The learned High Court Government Pleader for the respondent No.1 - State, reiterated the submissions made by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 - de - facto complainant.
Considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and the charge sheet material.

08. Perusal of the charge-sheet material indicates that, there is no specific allegations against accused No.2 and 3, as to how and in what manner they subjected the de-facto - complainant to cruelty both mentally and physically.

The specific allegations are made, against the accused No.1.
09.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Kahkashan Kausar v. State of Bihar, reported in (2022) 6 SCC 599, at Para No.18, has held as under :-
"18.

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar v. State of Bihar, reported in (2022) 6 SCC 599
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The above-mentioned decisions clearly demonstrate that this court has at numerous instances expressed concern over the misuse of section 498A IPC and the increased tendency of implicating relatives of the husband in matrimonial disputes,
without analysing the long term ramifications of a trial on the complainant as well as the accused.

It is further manifest from the said judgments that false implication by way of general omnibus allegations made in the course of matrimonial dispute, if left unchecked would result in misuse of the process of law.
Therefore, this court by way of its judgments has warned the courts from proceeding against the relatives and in-laws of the husband when no prima facie case is made out against them."
Hence, the cognizance taken by the learned Magistrate, as against the accused Nos.2 and 3 only on the basis of omnibus and general allegations, is impermissible in law.
Therefore, the continuation of criminal proceedings against the accused Nos.2 and 3, will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following;
ORDER I.
The petition against the petitioner - accused No.1, is hereby dismissed.
II. The petition against the petitioners - accused Nos.2 and 3, is herby allowed.
